newsitem.title: USA: WebTV, On Command aim to bring Internet to hotels.
newsitem.headline: WebTV, On Command aim to bring Internet to hotels.

text.p: Travelling hotel guests may soon get the chance to surf the World Wide Web from their beds using a high-speed Internet connection.

WebTV Networks and On Command Corp said Tuesday they will collaborate on an effort to develop an enhanced version of the WebTV Network online service customised for use by business travelers and holiday guests alike.

Robert Kavner, the former AT&T Corp executive who now is president and CEO of On Command, said the goal is to develop a service which can "bring people into the Internet experience in a delightful and friendly way."

"The audience for this ranges from the first time user all the way up to a heavy Internet surfer," he said. "We want to set this up in a way so its an invitation for people to take their first e-ticket ride on the Internet."

Kavner said that after a three-month trial in selected San Francisco area hotels, the companies hope to develop a service which will can be deployed in hotels beyond the nearly one million rooms On Command already serves.
The companies declined to disclose the size of their investments in the project, or to elaborate on their plans to eventually share in proceeds from the new service.

WebTV President and CEO Steve Perlman said the system will take advantage of very high speed communications lines that can be run into hotels and shared among a large number of rooms, so it will exceed the performance of dialup access.
"You're actually going to get a much more exciting presentation in the hotel room than pretty much anywhere else," he said in a conference call with analysts and media.
Kavner declined to give details on pricing, saying a variety of different models will be evaluated.

Users will be able to send and receive electronic mail, and depending on how the systems are deployed they may be able to either check into their own e-mail accounts with public providers or have electronic mail forwarded after their stay.

Perlman said the custom version of WebTV being developed for hotels will use an Ethernet connection, rather than modems, and would be deployed through On Command devices already used for services like games and movies-on demand.
"All we have to do is go in and swap out a remote control and add a keyboard...the rest of it happens behind the scenes," Perlman said of the new service.

"If you know how to use a remote control, you know how to use WebTV," said Perlman, adding the existing WebTV Network has achieved a 97 percent satisfaction rate, according to surveys of initial users since it was rolled out last Fall.
